claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a front suspension fork and a rear coil shock absorber.
The witness report states the specific frame size or wheel diameter was not shown.
The witness saw the frame but structural integrity (cracks/welds) was not shown.
The witness saw knobby tires but noted that wear levels and air retention were not shown.
The witness report explicitly states functionality of brakes and gear shifting was not shown.
The report does not confirm the movement of the saddle or suspension components.

risks.risk: Mechanical failure of the gear system (derailleur, shifters, or cables).
risks.proof: A video clip showing the bike being pedaled while shifting through every gear smoothly.
risks.if_unproven: As a single-speed bike requiring a full gear system overhaul.

risks.risk: Brake system failure or seized calipers.
risks.proof: A video showing the wheels spinning freely and then coming to a complete stop when the brakes are applied.
risks.if_unproven: As having non-functional brakes requiring replacement.

risks.risk: Structural frame damage or hidden cracks/repairs.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all frame joints, the bottom bracket area, and the underside of the down tube.
risks.if_unproven: As a damaged frame with scrap-only value.

risks.risk: Worn drivetrain components (stretched chain or shark-finned teeth on cassette).
risks.proof: Clear, close-up photos of the rear cassette teeth and the front chainrings.
risks.if_unproven: As requiring a full drivetrain replacement (chain and cassette).

risks.proof: A video showing the front fork and rear shock compressing and rebounding under weight.
risks.if_unproven: As a rigid frame with dead weight suspension.

proof_requests: A video of the bike being ridden, demonstrating gear shifting and braking.
Close-up photos of the tire sidewalls to confirm the '26' size and rubber condition.
Close-up photos of the rear derailleur and the teeth on the rear gears.
Close-up photos of the frame welds to check for cracks or DIY repairs.
response.reason: The witness has clearly identified the item as a KONEKT dual-suspension mountain bike. It can be priced at its worst-case functional condition until mechanical claims are proven.
